title: Coco and Nimbus's Sleepy Yawn Rescue
markdown:
In a wide fluffy meadow lived a little lamb named Coco and a cloud pony named Nimbus. They were the best of friends. They had the most important job in the whole wide meadow. They were like the secret sleepy-time helpers of the fluffy fields.

Coco was a little lamb. His wool was so fluffy, it looked like a cloud. A bouncy cloud. When he walked, his wool bounced. It jiggled. It made happy waves. Coco did not say baa-humbug. Coco hummed happy little baa-hums all day long. It sounded like tiny bells tinkling. And Nimbus was a cloud pony. He was all soft and white and bouncy, like a giant freshly baked marshmallow you could ride on. His hooves did not go clop-clop on the ground. They went more like a gentle poof-poof. He floated along, barely tickling the grass. His mane shimmered with rainbow sprinkles after a nice sprinkle-y rain shower. Then it would catch the sunlight and sparkle like tiny disco balls. It was quite a sight.

Now, these two had a secret mission. You see, the littlest lambs, the tiny ones who were just learning to hop and skip, sometimes had trouble getting to sleep. They’d wiggle their little bottoms and fidget their tiny legs. Their eyes would stay wide open, like saucers. Well, Coco and Nimbus knew just what to do. They collected sleepy yawns. It’s like collecting giggles or happy sighs, but for sleepy-time.

Every afternoon, when the sun was warm and lazy, it made the buttercups glow like little golden coins. The flowers were snoozing under its gentle rays. Then Coco and Nimbus would tiptoe through the meadow. Coco had a super-duper sniffy nose. It was the kind that could smell a tasty daisy from ages away. Sniff, sniff. His little nose would twitch. “Ah-ha,” he’d bleat softly. His voice was like a tiny bell. And Nimbus, with his gentle cloud-pony magic, would float over to a snoozing lamb. He’d hover just above them. His cloudy body cast a soft cool shadow. They would not wake them. That would be a big no-no. They’d just hover close, like a friendly whisper.

And when a little lamb let out a big soft yawwwn, Coco was ready. He’d spread his fluffy wool, making a little scooping shape. And Nimbus would carefully guide the yawn right into Coco’s woolly embrace. Poof. The yawn would get all sparkly and soft, like catching a falling star. “Gotcha,” Nimbus would whisper. His voice was like a soft breeze rustling through the tall grass. They collected yawns that felt like warm hugs and cosy blankets. Some yawns were little squeaky ones, like a mouse’s sigh. Some were great big stretch-y ones that made your whole body want to wiggle. The big ones went like a little gust of sleepy air. They were all different shapes and sizes, but all wonderfully sleepy.

Then they’d take all the sleepy yawns, all the sparkly, soft, huggy yawns, back to their special little place. It wasn’t a big building. It was a tiny secret hut tucked away behind a patch of shimmering moon-petal flowers. It was made of sunshine and daisy petals, and it always smelled like fresh cookies and happy dreams. And with soft fluffy threads that Nimbus spun from moonbeams, they’d stitch all the yawns together. They stitched and stitched and stitched. Their little hooves and woolly paws worked together in perfect rhythm. “A little bit of this yawn here,” Coco would say, carefully placing a small shimmering yawn. “And a big fluffy one from that sleepyhead over there.” It was like sewing with clouds, only much cosier. And slowly, slowly, a beautiful drifting blanket began to grow. It wasn’t made of wool or cotton. It was made of pure sleepiness and happy dreams. It had swirls of soft colours from the yawns, and a gentle sparkle from the moonbeam threads.

When the blanket was finished, it was the most wonderfully soft thing you ever did see. It was light as a whisper. It drifted like a dandelion seed on the wind. It shimmered gently in the afternoon sun, promising sweet dreams. They would tiptoe to the littlest lambs’ napping spots. Those were the spots where the babies were still trying their hardest to stay awake. Their eyelids were just a tiny bit droopy. And very, very gently, with Nimbus floating it and Coco guiding it, they would lay the sleepy yawn blanket over them. It felt like the softest hug ever.

The moment the blanket touched their woolly backs, you could see the little lambs relax. Their wiggles stopped. Their fidgets faded away like mist. And their eyes would flutter shut. They’d be fast asleep. Their little lamby snores were soft and sweet. They were dreaming of bouncing buttercups and tasty clover fields. And Coco and Nimbus would smile at each other. Their hearts were full of the warm cosy feeling of a job well done. They didn’t need a thank you, because they could see the peaceful sleep on the little lambs’ faces. Then they floated home behind the moon-petal flowers, ready for a yawn of their own.
